> **What this case shows** — the ecosystem's complexity measures read *amplitudes*, *template matches*,
> or *1-D symbol sequences*. **Phase entropy** (Rohila & Sharma 2019) reads the signal's *phase-plane
> geometry*: it plots each first difference against the following second difference — the **Second-Order
> Difference Plot (SODP)** — and takes the entropy of the polar-angle distribution over *k* sectors.
> This case introduces a **newly-authored op**, `phaseEntropy`. On a real eyes-closed EEG channel it
> reproduces `NeuroKit2.entropy_phase` **bit-for-bit** (max |diff| ~**4e-16**).

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — `phaseEntropy(x, delay, k)` → the phase entropy of the SODP.
**Way of thinking** — velocity and acceleration together define a phase plane. Where a point lands in
that plane (its angle) says whether the signal is speeding up, slowing, reversing; the entropy of those
angles is a compact measure of how varied the local dynamics are.
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioEEG::phaseEntropy()` alongside the amplitude, template and symbolic
complexity ops — a phase-plane-geometry mechanism they don't have.
:::

## Proposition

On real eyes-closed POz EEG, `phaseEntropy` reproduces `NeuroKit2.entropy_phase` bit-for-bit (max |diff|
~4e-16) across the sector count k; PhasEn increases with k (1.238 → 1.287 → 1.299) and sits below the
1/ln(2) = 1.443 normalization ceiling.

## Question & goal

**The question is a gap and a domain: the ecosystem's complexity measures read amplitude or symbol
sequences — can we author the phase-plane (SODP) entropy, reproduce the reference, and characterize the
angular structure?** The goal is to introduce `phaseEntropy`, certify it bit-for-bit, and read the SODP.

## Challenge & approach

Phase entropy forms the SODP (first difference x(n+τ)−x(n) against second difference
x(n+2τ)−x(n+τ)), takes each point's quadrant-corrected polar angle, bins it into k equal sectors of
[0, 2π), and takes the normalized Shannon entropy of the angle-weighted sector distribution. We
implement that exactly and check it against `NeuroKit2.entropy_phase` across k.

```
EEG POz (eegmmidb) → SODP (Δx vs Δ²x) → polar angle → k sectors → normalized Shannon(sector mass)
                    vs NeuroKit2.entropy_phase (same pipeline) → bit-exact (~4e-16) for every k
                    increases with k (1.24 → 1.29 → 1.30);  below the 1/ln2 = 1.443 ceiling
```

## Data

**EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb, PhysioNet)**: subject **S002**, run **R02
(eyes-closed)**, channel **POz**, 10 s at 160 Hz — the same git-tracked vector the
[dispersion](../dispersion-entropy-eegmmidb/index.qmd), [increment](../increment-entropy-eegmmidb/index.qmd)
and [slope](../slope-entropy-eegmmidb/index.qmd) entropy cases use. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| **PhasEn, k = 4** (delay 1) | **1.238** |
| **PhasEn, k = 6** | **1.287** |
| **PhasEn, k = 8** | **1.299** |
| op vs `NeuroKit2.entropy_phase` (max \|diff\| over k) | **4e-16** (bit-exact) |
| increasing in k | **yes** |
| below ceiling 1/ln(2) = 1.443 | **yes** |

The newly-authored op equals NeuroKit2 at every k, and the SODP + increasing family characterize the
phase-plane structure. Values trace to
[`artifacts/phase_summary.csv`](artifacts/phase_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`phaseEntropy` adds a mechanism the ecosystem's entropies did not have — phase-plane geometry via the
SODP — and it is exact: bit-for-bit against NeuroKit2 across k. The transferable takeaway: **the SODP
turns a time series into a velocity–acceleration cloud; its angular entropy is a compact, geometry-aware
complexity that complements the amplitude and symbolic measures — reach for it when the dynamics, not
the levels, carry the information.**

## Open questions

- Phase entropy was introduced for HRV; applying it to the RR-interval SODP (not EEG) across autonomic
  states, and sweeping k as a resolution knob, would connect this op to its original clinical use.
  *Documented, not escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| Phase entropy (SODP geometry) | `phaseEntropy()` | PhysioEEG |
| Slope entropy (trend shape) | `slopeEntropy()` | PhysioEEG |
| Increment entropy (change magnitude) | `incrementEntropy()` | PhysioEEG |
| Dispersion entropy (amplitude patterns) | `dispersionEntropy()` | PhysioEEG |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **delay** — lag for both differences (default 1); larger delays probe slower dynamics on the SODP.
- **k** — number of angular sectors (default 4); more sectors resolve finer angular structure and raise
  PhasEn toward its ceiling.
- **units** — dimensionless; the NeuroKit2 normalization (base-2 Shannon / ln k) bounds PhasEn in
  [0, 1/ln2 = 1.443].

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioEEG)

phaseEntropy(x, delay = 1, k = 4)   # SODP phase entropy
# reproduces NeuroKit2.entropy_phase bit-for-bit across the sector count k.
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/phase_summary.csv`](artifacts/phase_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks
PhasEn at k = 4, 6, 8, the bit-exact NeuroKit2 match over k, the increase with k, the normalization
ceiling, and the honestly-noted scope (newly-authored op; machine-precision; NeuroKit2 normalization
reproduced; value depends on delay/k).
